celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الْمُدَّثِّرُ﴾ the Prophet ﷺ; its underlying form is الْمُتَدَثِّرُ, with the tāʾ assimilated into the dāl, i.e. the one wrapped in his garments when the revelation came down upon him.

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿قُمْ فَأَنْذِرْ﴾ make the people of Mecca fear the Fire if they do not believe,

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿وَرَبَّكَ فَكَبِّرْ﴾ magnify [Him] above the associating of partners by the idolaters,

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿وَثِيَابَكَ فَطَهِّرْ﴾ from impurity; or shorten them, unlike the Arabs' trailing of their garments out of pride, since impurity might then strike them,

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿وَالرُّجْزَ﴾ the Prophet ﷺ explained it as the idols ﴿فَاهْجُرْ﴾ i.e. persist in shunning it,

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿وَلَا تَمْنُنْ تَسْتَكْثِرُ﴾ in the nominative, a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. do not give something in order to seek more than it; and this is particular to him ﷺ, because he was commanded with the finest character and the noblest manners;

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿وَلِرَبِّكَ فَاصْبِرْ﴾ in [keeping] the commands and prohibitions.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿فَإِذَا نُقِرَ فِي النَّاقُورِ﴾ the trumpet is blown, which is the horn — the second blowing —

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿فَذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. the time of the blowing ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ a badal (substitute) for what precedes it, the mubtadaʾ (subject); it is indeclinable (mabnī) because it is annexed to something not fully declinable (ghayr mutamakkin); and the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ is ﴿يَوْمٌ عَسِيرٌ﴾; what governs إِذَا is what the clause indicates, i.e. the matter became severe,

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ غَيْرُ يَسِيرٍ﴾ this indicates that it is easy for the believers, i.e. despite its hardship.

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿ذَرْنِي﴾ leave Me ﴿وَمَنْ خَلَقْتُ﴾ conjoined to the object, or a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment) ﴿وَحِيدًا﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) from مَنْ, or from its pronoun omitted from خَلَقْتُ, i.e. alone, with neither family nor wealth; he is al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra al-Makhzūmī;

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿وَجَعَلْتُ لَهُ مَالًا مَمْدُودًا﴾ extensive and continuous, of crops, livestock and trade,

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿وَبَنِينَ﴾ ten or more ﴿شُهُودًا﴾ who attend gatherings and whose testimony is heard,

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿وَمَهَّدْتُ﴾ I spread out ﴿لَهُ﴾ in livelihood, lifespan and children ﴿تَمْهِيدًا﴾

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿ثُمَّ يَطْمَعُ أَنْ أَزِيدَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here]

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ I will not give him more than that; ﴿إِنَّهُ كَانَ لِآيَاتِنَا﴾ i.e. the Quran ﴿عَنِيدًا﴾ obstinately opposed.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿سَأُرْهِقُهُ﴾ I will impose on him ﴿صَعُودًا﴾ a hardship of punishment, or a mountain of fire which he climbs and then falls down from, forever.

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿إِنَّهُ فَكَّرَ﴾ about what to say regarding the Quran that he had heard from the Prophet ﷺ ﴿وَقَدَّرَ﴾ that in himself.

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿فَقُتِلَ﴾ may he be cursed and punished; ﴿كَيْفَ قَدَّرَ﴾ in whatever state his deliberation was;

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿ثُمَّ قُتِلَ كَيْفَ قَدَّرَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here]

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿ثُمَّ نَظَرَ﴾ at the faces of his people, or at what he might use to disparage it,

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿ثُمَّ عَبَسَ﴾ contracted and grimaced his face, being frustrated about what to say, ﴿وَبَسَرَ﴾ increased in contracting and grimacing,

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿ثُمَّ أَدْبَرَ﴾ from faith ﴿وَاسْتَكْبَرَ﴾ was too proud to follow the Prophet ﷺ,

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿فَقَالَ﴾ about what he brought: ﴿إِنْ﴾ not ﴿هَذَا إِلَّا سِحْرٌ يُؤْثَرُ﴾ transmitted from sorcerers;

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿إِنْ﴾ not ﴿هَذَا إِلَّا قَوْلُ الْبَشَرِ﴾ as they said: "It is only a human being who teaches him."

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿سَأُصْلِيهِ﴾ I will make him enter ﴿سَقَرَ﴾ Hell.

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا سَقَرُ﴾ magnifying its import.

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿لَا تُبْقِي وَلَا تَذَرُ﴾ any flesh or sinew without destroying it; then it returns as it was.

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿عَلَيْهَا تِسْعَةَ عَشَرَ﴾ angels, its keepers. One of the unbelievers, who was strong and of great might, said: "I will take care of seventeen for you, and you take care of two for me." Allah the Exalted said:

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿وَمَا جَعَلْنَا أَصْحَابَ النَّارِ إِلَّا مَلَائِكَةً﴾ i.e. so they cannot be overpowered, as they imagine; ﴿وَمَا جَعَلْنَا عِدَّتَهُمْ﴾ that ﴿إِلَّا فِتْنَةً﴾ a misguidance ﴿لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ in that they say: why are they nineteen? ﴿لِيَسْتَيْقِنَ﴾ that they may be clear about it ﴿الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ﴾ i.e. the Jews, that the Prophet ﷺ spoke the truth about their being nineteen, which agrees with what is in their scripture; ﴿وَيَزْدَادَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ of the People of the Book ﴿إِيمَانًا﴾ belief, because what the Prophet ﷺ brought agrees with what is in their scripture; ﴿وَلَا يَرْتَابَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ others besides them, concerning the number of the angels; ﴿وَلِيَقُولَ الَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ﴾ doubt, in Medina, ﴿وَالْكَافِرُونَ﴾ in Mecca: ﴿مَاذَا أَرَادَ اللَّهُ بِهَذَا﴾ number ﴿مَثَلًا﴾ they called it that because of its strangeness, and it is parsed as a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. like the misguiding of the one who rejects this number and the guiding of the one who accepts it ﴿يُضِلُّ اللَّهُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَيَهْدِي مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَمَا يَعْلَمُ جُنُودَ رَبِّكَ﴾ i.e. the angels, in their strength and their helpers, ﴿إِلَّا هُوَ وَمَا هِيَ﴾ i.e. Saqar ﴿إِلَّا ذِكْرَى لِلْبَشَرِ﴾

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ an opening particle (istiftāḥ) in the sense of أَلَا; ﴿وَالْقَمَرِ﴾

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا﴾ with fatḥa on the dhāl ﴿دَبَرَ﴾ came after the day; in one reading [إِذْ أَدْبَرَ] with sukūn on the dhāl followed by a hamza, i.e. passed away;

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿إِنَّهَا﴾ i.e. Saqar ﴿لَإِحْدَى الْكُبَرِ﴾ the great calamities,

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿نَذِيرًا﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) from إِحْدَى; it is masculine because it is in the sense of "the punishment"; ﴿لِلْبَشَرِ﴾

celaleyn:37-37.t: ﴿لِمَنْ شَاءَ مِنْكُمْ﴾ a badal (substitute) for الْبَشَرِ ﴿أَنْ يَتَقَدَّمَ﴾ to good, or to Paradise, through faith, ﴿أَوْ يَتَأَخَّرَ﴾ to evil, or to the Fire, through unbelief.

celaleyn:38-38.t: ﴿كُلُّ نَفْسٍ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ رَهِينَةٌ﴾ pledged, held in the Fire for its deeds,

celaleyn:39-39.t: ﴿إِلَّا أَصْحَابَ الْيَمِينِ﴾ and they are the believers, who are saved from it, being

celaleyn:41-41.t: ﴿عَنِ الْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾ and their state, and they say to them, after the monotheists have been taken out of the Fire:

celaleyn:43-43.t: ﴿قَالُوا لَمْ نَكُ مِنَ الْمُصَلِّينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here]

celaleyn:44-44.t: ﴿وَلَمْ نَكُ نُطْعِمُ الْمِسْكِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here]

celaleyn:46-46.t: ﴿وَكُنَّا نُكَذِّبُ بِيَوْمِ الدِّينِ﴾ the resurrection and the recompense,

celaleyn:48-48.t: ﴿فَمَا تَنْفَعُهُمْ شَفَاعَةُ الشَّافِعِينَ﴾ of the angels, the prophets and the righteous; the meaning is: they have no intercession.

celaleyn:49-49.t: ﴿فَمَا﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ its khabar (predicate), attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted [word] whose pronoun has moved to it; ﴿عَنِ التَّذْكِرَةِ مُعْرِضِينَ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun; the meaning is: what has come over them in their turning away from taking admonition?

celaleyn:51-51.t: ﴿فَرَّتْ مِنْ قَسْوَرَةٍ﴾ a lion, i.e. fled from it in the most intense flight.

celaleyn:52-52.t: ﴿بَلْ يُرِيدُ كُلُّ امْرِئٍ مِنْهُمْ أَنْ يُؤْتَى صُحُفًا مُنَشَّرَةً﴾ i.e. from Allah the Exalted, [commanding them] to follow the Prophet, as they said: "We will not believe in you until you bring down to us a book we can read."

celaleyn:53-53.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ a deterrent from what they wanted; ﴿بَلْ لَا يَخَافُونَ الْآخِرَةَ﴾ i.e. its punishment.

celaleyn:54-54.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ an opening particle (istiftāḥ); ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ i.e. the Quran ﴿تَذْكِرَةٌ﴾ an admonition;

celaleyn:55-55.t: ﴿فَمَنْ شَاءَ ذَكَرَهُ﴾ read it and took admonition from it.

celaleyn:56-56.t: ﴿وَمَا يَذْكُرُونَ﴾ with yāʾ and with tāʾ ﴿إِلَّا أَنْ يَشَاءَ اللَّهُ هُوَ أَهْلُ التَّقْوَى﴾ [worthy] of being feared ﴿وَأَهْلُ الْمَغْفِرَةِ﴾ [worthy] of forgiving whoever fears Him.
